---
title: "Installation"
---




MINTverse is two packages, `estimint`, which maps a measured prevalence to transmission
intensity, and `stateMINT`, which emulates the prevalence and case trajectories that
follow an intervention. Install both:

```bash
pip install estimint mintstate
```

The equivalent inside a project managed by [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), rather than
a bare environment, is:

```bash
uv add estimint mintstate
```

Python 3.12 or newer is required, since both packages declare it. Neither will install
on an older interpreter.

::: {.callout-note}
## The distribution name is not the import name

`stateMINT` is published on PyPI as **`mintstate`**, so you install `mintstate` and you
import `stateMINT`:

```python
import stateMINT          # correct
import mintstate          # ModuleNotFoundError
```

`estimint` has no such split, and the distribution and the module are both `estimint`.
:::

`pip install "estimint[scenarios]"` installs the same two packages, because that extra
declares `mintstate` as a dependency. It adds nothing else.

## Extras

An extra is an optional set of dependencies, named in square brackets after the package,
and `estimint` on its own provides the EIR and HBR models and nothing else. It has no
emulator. Without one it cannot produce trajectories, and the remaining extras are only
needed if you are refitting the models or want the bundled plotting helpers.

| Extra | Command | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `scenarios` | `pip install "estimint[scenarios]"` | `stateMINT`, the same as naming `mintstate` yourself. |
| `viz` | `pip install "estimint[viz]"` | matplotlib, for the bundled plotting helpers. |
| `download` | `pip install "estimint[download]"` | The fetchers used to pull training data. |
| `train` | `pip install "estimint[train]"` | duckdb, scikit-learn and pyarrow, for refitting the XGBoost models. |
| `all` | `pip install "estimint[all]"` | All four of the above. |

`stateMINT` carries a single extra, for machines with an NVIDIA GPU:

| Extra | Command | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| `gpu` | `pip install "mintstate[gpu]"` | `jax[cuda12]`, so the emulator runs on an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12. |

The emulator runs on JAX, and the CPU build is fast enough for inference. A ten-scenario
batch takes about a second. A GPU is worth installing if you are training, or sweeping a
grid of thousands.

## Where the weights live

`estimint` ships its three XGBoost models (prevalence, HBR and EIR-to-HBR) inside the
wheel, so `load_xgb_model("prevalence")` reads a file that is already on disk. It never
needs a network.

`stateMINT` does need a network on first use, because its checkpoints live in the
Hugging Face repository [`dide-ic/stateMINT`](https://huggingface.co/dide-ic/stateMINT),
with a separately trained checkpoint for each predictor under `prevalence/` and
`cases/`. The first call that needs one fetches it and caches it under
`~/.cache/huggingface`, and every later call reads the cache. Each predictor is about
38 MB. The first `run_scenarios` of a new install therefore needs a working network, and
is slower than every one that follows.

Warm both caches up front so that the download does not land in the middle of a session.
`preload_models()` loads the XGBoost models and pulls the stateMINT weights:

```python
from estimint import preload_models

preload_models()
```

## Working offline

On a cluster node or an air-gapped machine, warm the cache somewhere with a network
first, then set `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` so Hugging Face never attempts a request and resolves
everything from `~/.cache/huggingface`:

```bash
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
```

If the cache directory itself is unavailable, put the weights somewhere you control and
load them from a path, since `from_pretrained` takes a `local_dir` and will read a
directory laid out like the repository instead of calling the Hub:

```python
from stateMINT.model import Mamba2Regressor

artifact = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained(
    "dide-ic/stateMINT",
    predictor="prevalence",
    revision="v1.2.2",
    local_dir="/shared/models/stateMINT",
)
```

## Verify

`importlib.metadata` reports the version of an installed distribution rather than of an
imported module, so the emulator's version is recorded under `mintstate` and not under
`stateMINT`. `net_types()` asks `estimint` which net formulations it knows about.

::: {#0bf78bcd .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import importlib.metadata as md

import estimint
import stateMINT

print("estimint  (import estimint) ", md.version("estimint"))
print("mintstate (import stateMINT)", md.version("mintstate"))
print()
print("net types:", estimint.net_types())
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
estimint  (import estimint)  1.5.4
mintstate (import stateMINT) 0.3.1

net types: ['pyrethroid_only', 'pyrethroid_pbo', 'pyrethroid_ppf', 'pyrethroid_pyrrole']
```
:::
:::


Four net formulations and no error confirms that both packages are installed correctly.
